judge_assessment.explanation: Every arithmetic claim the judge makes is correct and I reproduced all twelve independently: -8+3=-5, -6-(-11)=5, (-4)(7)=-28, -1 < -3/4 < -0.6 < 1/2, -3+4(-2)=-11, (-3/4)(8/9)=-24/36=-2/3, 2.5+(-7.25)=-4.75, -5/6=-0.8333... < -0.8, (-2)^3+12/(-4)=-8-3=-11, -24/(-6)*(-2)=4*(-2)=-8, -3(2-5)-16/8=9-2=7, and the descending order -2.05 > -9/4 > -2.5 > -11/4. Two things the judge did not look at fail. First, the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints "8. —" for problem 8, whose verify.json entry is a VERIFIED compare with expected "<"; sympify cannot parse "<", so _fmt's except branch returns the em dash that render_entry also uses for manual-only ids, and a grader cannot tell a checked answer from an unchecked one. Second, the judge recorded manual_items_reviewed 0, which matches verify.json (no manual entries) and gate_chain_manual_flags false — but problems 5, 8, 10 and 12 all demand written reasoning on the sheet ("Which operation has to happen first, and why?", "say how you decided", "Find her mistake", "explain in one sentence"), and final_response.md states "Nothing is flagged for manual review" two paragraphs before conceding that problems 5, 8 and 12 ask for sentences that "are not machine-checked". The prompt asked for open responses to be clearly labelled; they are not.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10's error analysis is the model to copy: the planted wrong answer -2 is declared as a trap whose expr a/(b*c) is built from the problem's OWN givens, so verify.py proved the misconception really produces -2 while the correct left-to-right reading gives -8, and the key's "What Priya did wrong" line names the rule (equal-rank operations are never reordered) rather than just marking the answer.

Every key solution carries a "Listen for" line naming the specific wrong answer that problem produces (-11 for -8+3, -17 for -6-(-11), -0.6 < -0.75 from ordering negatives as if positive), which turns grading into diagnosis.
Problem 9's key does not stop at -11: it adds that (-2)^3 and -2^3 agree while (-2)^2 and -2^2 do not, which is the exact boundary a seventh grader gets wrong next.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt routes every string expected through bare sympy.sympify and treats a SympifyError as "no answer", collapsing a verified relation into the same em dash used for manual-only items.
evidence: verify.json id 8: {"type": "compare", "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} — machine-verified, gate verify-ws PASS.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints "8. —" while the worked solution on page 2 boxes -5/6 < -0.8.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61: the except branch returns "---", identical to render_entry's manual-only return.

root_causes.description: Nothing in the contract couples an open-response demand printed in the worksheet stem to a manual entry in verify.json, so a sheet with four written-reasoning prompts can pass every gate reporting zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problems 5, 8, 10 and 12 each ask for a sentence of reasoning in addition to a value.
verify.json declares 12 machine entries and no {"type": "manual"} entry at all.
gate_log.txt ends "BUILD PASSED — all gates green"; the machine observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false.
final_response.md: "Nothing is flagged for manual review", then "those sentences are not machine-checked" in the same paragraph.

improvements.title: Render verified relation symbols in the Quick Answers bank instead of the manual-only em dash
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, match relation strings ("<", ">", "=", "<=", ">=", "!=") BEFORE calling sympify and emit the typeset symbol ($<$, $\le$, ...). sympify("<") raises SympifyError and the except branch returns "---", the same glyph render_entry reserves for manual-only ids, so a verified relation and an unchecked item are indistinguishable in the delivered bank.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: render a verify JSON holding a {"type": "compare", "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} entry and assert the bank line is "2.~$<$" and that "---" appears only on ids whose entries carry no "expected". Fails today (the line renders "---").
improvements.expected_impact: Every compare/relation problem across the suite regains a readable bank entry, and the em dash goes back to meaning exactly one thing: nobody machine-checked this. On this sheet, problem 8's bank entry becomes $<$ instead of the — that currently sits beside eleven real answers.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one branch of _fmt; the only care needed is escaping the symbols for LaTeX math mode so "<" does not compile as a stray glyph.

improvements.title: Fail the build when a problem stem asks for reasoning and its verify entry is machine-only
improvements.proposed_change: Add a delivery-blocking lint that pairs the worksheet source with the verify JSON: scan each \problem block for an open-response demand ("explain", "say why", "say how you decided", "in one sentence", "what went wrong", "find her mistake", "describe", "sketch", "plot", "graph it") and fail the build when that problem id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. SKILL.md should state the rule positively: a problem that asks for a value AND a sentence gets TWO verify entries, the machine one for the value and a manual one carrying the full-credit criteria, exactly as this run already does elsewhere.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pair under tests/fixtures: a worksheet .tex whose problem 3 stem ends "Explain in one sentence why ..." beside a verify.json whose id 3 holds only an eval entry. tests/check_prose_consistency.py must exit non-zero naming problem 3; adding {"id": 3, "type": "manual", "desc": ...} makes it exit 0. The test fails today because no checker reads the stem for open-response prose.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate chain's manual-flag count starts telling the truth, so a grader is told which written answers nobody machine-checked instead of reading "nothing is flagged for manual review" under a sheet full of explanation prompts. On curr-170 the manual count moves from 0 to 4 (problems 5, 8, 10, 12) and final_response.md stops contradicting itself.
improvements.risk: Keyword matching will flag stems whose imperative is decorative ("show your work"), so the lint needs a curated phrase list and an explicit per-problem opt-out, or authors will start declaring hollow manual entries to silence it.

case_summary: A mathematically flawless interleaved signed-number review: twelve problems rotating add/subtract, multiply/divide, ordering and order-of-operations, with a genuine warm-up, a machine-checked error-analysis item at 10 and a close ordering challenge at 12. I recomputed all twelve answers and both orderings and found no error; the study guide's four sections mirror the four facets and its try-its (-7-(-2)=-5, -45/9=-5, -7/8 < -0.85, -5+36/(-9)=-9) all check. Two delivery defects survive the green gate chain. The Quick Answers bank prints an em dash for problem 8's verified "<", which is the glyph the same bank uses for items nobody checked, so a grader cannot distinguish them. And the sheet declares zero manual items while four problems demand written reasoning, against a prompt that explicitly asked for open responses to be labelled.
